title: Find a grant for your small business

paragraphs: Info Page
Learn about current City-run grant options for your business.
Sign up for emails from the Office of Small Business to get updates on grant programs.

sections.heading: Grants with rolling deadlines › Accessible Barrier Removal
paragraphs: Small businesses can receive up to $10,000 in reimbursement for eligible accessibility improvements that help make their storefronts more accessible to the public and support compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).
Learn more about the Accessible Barrier Removal Grant , then apply here .

sections.heading: Grants with rolling deadlines › Disaster Relief
paragraphs: Small businesses can receive up to $10,000 in grant funding to help recover and reopen after a major fire or vehicular accident.
Learn more about the Disaster Relief Grant

sections.heading: Grants with rolling deadlines › Vacant to Vibrant
paragraphs: Participating entrepreneurs receive grants and technical assistance such as lease negotiations, permit support, insurance, and marketing for new pop-up locations in downtown San Francisco. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
Learn more about Vacant to Vibrant , then apply here .

sections.heading: Grants with rolling deadlines › Floodwater management
paragraphs: This program is run by SFPUC, for properties that experience flooding from the sewer system or adjacent public right-of-way caused by heavy rains.
Learn more about the Floodwater Management Grant

sections.heading: Grants with rolling deadlines › Businesses over 30 years old
paragraphs: Long-standing small businesses can join the Legacy Business Registry for recognition, marketing and business help, and special grants.
Learn more about the Legacy Business Program

sections.heading: Grants with rolling deadlines › Automatic dishwashing grant
paragraphs: Grants of up to $2,500 toward leasing or buying automatic dishwashers, to help food service businesses build reusable foodware infrastructure for on-site dining. Priority given to businesses that do not currently have a dishwasher and are ready to transition from disposable to reusable foodware for on-site dining.
Learn more about the Automatic Dishwashing Grant

sections.heading: Grants with rolling deadlines › Commercial Washer Rebate
paragraphs: This program from SFPUC provides a rebate of up to $1,000 for the purchase of eligible commercial grade clothes washers in laundromats.
Learn more about the rebate program

sections.heading: Communities › Community and neighborhood improvement
paragraphs: Find funding for projects that improve neighborhoods. Grantees can be nonprofit organizations; businesses, community groups, and schools that do not have their nonprofit status may apply through a fiscal sponsor that is a nonprofit organization.
Learn more about Community Challenge Grants

sections.heading: Communities › Low-income communities
paragraphs: Get help with projects that offer community benefits in low-income neighborhoods.
Learn about the San Francisco Community Investment Fund

sections.heading: Communities › Arts
paragraphs: Find funding to support artists, art organizations, parades, and festivals.
Apply for arts funding from Grants for the Arts
Apply for arts funding from the San Francisco Arts Commission

sections.heading: Closed grants (for reference only) › SF Shines Facade Improvement Grant - now closed
paragraphs: Businesses with eligible facade beautification projects can receive a grant of up to $20,000. While now closed, you can learn more about the SF Shines Facade Improvement grant .

sections.heading: Closed grants (for reference only) › SF Shines Interior Improvements Grant - now closed
paragraphs: Improve your business storefront or interior space with a SF Shines grant. Applications opened on February 28, 2025 and are now closed. Learn more about the SF Shines interior grant here.

sections.heading: Closed grants (for reference only) › SF Thrives Grant - now closed
paragraphs: Offering up to $10,000 in reimbursement grants for eligible operational expenses, the program supports small businesses in low- to moderate-income neighborhoods experiencing a slower post-pandemic rebound —helping them stabilize, reinvest, and thrive as part of San Francisco’s broader economic recovery.
Storefronts must have been operating on or before December 31, 2020 and had to close or limit operations during Shelter In Place (SIP) orders.
Learn more:
SOMA, Mid-Market, and Tenderloin
Western Addition
Treasure Island
Applications are now closed. All applicants will be notified of their award or non-award status by January 30, 2026.

sections.heading: Closed grants (for reference only) › SF Shines Equipment Grant - now closed
paragraphs: The SF Shines Equipment Grant supports commercially-zoned storefronts all over the City with up to $10,000 in funding for equipment purchases. The goal is to support long-term success and help our City's commercial corridors thrive.
Eligible equipment must support your business operations and align with one of the following purposes:
Start Up / Scale Up / Expand – To increase capacity, add new services, improve efficiency, or support growth
Remediation – To fix broken equipment that is limiting your ability to operate
Compliance – To resolve an open Notice of Violation (NOV) related to equipment in the interior of your storefront
Learn more about SF Shines Equipment Grant and apply here
SOG with broker services - now closed

Businesses in the Excelsior, Tenderloin, and Visitacion Valley can access comprehensive broker services, lease review services, and a $50,000 - $100,000 grant to open a new storefront. While now closed, you can learn more about the program .
